rationale.conceptual: The method is established (DFT with PW91, plane-wave basis, pseudopotentials) but requires careful implementation of a specific zeolite structure, aluminum substitution, Brønsted acidic site, and a multi-component approach: periodic DFT geometry optimization, energy extraction, and integration of a classical van der Waals correction from Deka et al. It is non-trivial and involves interacting components, but not a novel algorithm requiring deep research-grade insight.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves constructing the zeolite unit cell, running DFT optimizations of the bare zeolite, three xylene-zeolite complexes, and isolated xylene molecules (at least 7 separate calculations), then implementing a force-field correction from a literature reference. This is a multi-stage (~4-6 steps) pipeline with dependencies and one tricky tooling/environment step (installing Quantum ESPRESSO, extracting coordinates, applying force field). Data acquisition is straightforward (IZA database, published parameters).

difficulty.reasoning: Reproducing corrected adsorption energies requires periodic DFT geometry optimizations of zeolite-adsorbate complexes (146 atoms) using PW91 functional and plane-wave basis, plus a classical force-field correction. The method is standard but multi-step. Setup and execution involve building the cell, running multiple optimizations, and applying a literature force field. The task is conceptually moderate (established multi-part method) and executionally a pipeline with several stages and tool dependencies.

compute_estimate.reasoning: Periodic DFT calculation of a 146-atom unit cell with plane-wave cut-off 300 eV and Γ-point sampling; moderate memory usage (peak ~16 GB) and CPU time (~hours), no GPU required. Input data is negligible.
